newsitem.title: USA: Lehman to buy $1.23 bln loans from NCB.
newsitem.headline: Lehman to buy $1.23 bln loans from NCB.

text.p: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc said Thursday it has agreed to purchase a $1.23 billion portfolio of commercial loans from Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) in the largest secondary transaction in the history of syndicated lending.
The portfolio is made up of project finance and corporate loans made by Nippon Credit's New York office.

Christopher Ryan, managing director and head of the Lehman Brothers loan syndication and trading business, said the firm will use secondary markets and asset securitizations to wind down portions of the portfolio.

"The selection of Lehman Brothers as purchaser of this portfolio underscores the firm's capabilities in the commercial lending business," Michael O'Hanlon, managing director and head of the financial institutions investment banking practice said in a statement.
Ryan said the portfolio will bring Lehman additional relationship opportunities with certain borrowers.
Lehman Brothers started loan syndication and trading activities in 1992. The company said it has acted as agent or participated in more than $28 billion in loans in the past 12 months.
